answer.rationale: Write-path p99 is 5x at daily settlement peak with heavy writes. Rollback matched memory_b1 historically but is forbidden by the security-patch constraint, so it is off the table. memory_b4-style circuit breaking would fail fast and drop customer writes, which violates the objective. That leaves write-preserving mitigations. Heavy peak writes plus a release that may have made the path more expensive is most consistent with a headroom problem (memory_b3); failover (memory_b2) is the main alternative if this is regional degradation rather than load. Verifying those two records before lock-in. Intending add_capacity at standard—not broad—scale because the coincident release means the cause is still uncertain and a full-fleet move is not justified yet.
